- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks and shift toward lower end of range.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 5.0), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 2–3x the prior peak unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion occurs when forecast deviates >1.5σ from recent 7-day average; adjust toward historical mean unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates late-period (last 10 days) prices; apply downward bias of 10–15% for days 20–30 if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to overreact; smooth forecast curve with exponential decay filter (λ=0.7).
